label: copy phase, fed-back token in {n,u,p,w,q,k,2,o,a}, from the 3rd output on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L). It never fires during the original tokens, at <DEL>, or on the first copy step (recall_idx 0), and almost never at recall_idx 1. It needs the input to be a repeat, i.e. the model fed back a token it has already seen (in_first=0 always). Rate rises sharply with the identity of the fed-back input token: n, u, p, w, q, k, 2 have rates of 16-21% vs 5% baseline, then o and a; tokens such as l and s are low. It fires most at recall_idx 2-4 and near the end of long sequences, and is essentially silent when 7 or more outputs remain. Predicate (input token set, recall_idx>=2, to_go<=6) catches about 89% of activation mass on dev, but precision is only about 0.40. Even within the favoured tokens most steps are inactive, so some unidentified sequence-context factor gates it (no single prev_tok/out_tok condition fixed this). Coverage is higher for the top activation quartile, so the favoured input tokens also go with larger activations. Activation magnitudes are tiny overall (max 0.008).
